module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 285

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/285](https://www.erdosproblems.com/285)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

open scoped Topology Real

namespace Erdos285

/--
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ with
$$
  1 = \frac{1}{n_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
  f(k) = (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1} k ?
$$

Proved by Martin [Ma00].

[Ma00] Martin, Greg, _Denser Egyptian fractions_. Acta Arith. (2000), 231-260.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_285 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ᵉ (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (S : Set ℕ)
    (hS : S = {k | ∃ (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ), StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧
      1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i })
    (h : ∀ k ∈ S,
      IsLeast
        { n (Fin.last k) | (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n)
          (_ : 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i) }
        (f k)),
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
      ∀ k ∈ S, f k = (1 + o k) * rexp 1 / (rexp 1 - 1) * (k + 1) := by
  sorry

/--
It is trivial that $f(k)\geq (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1}k$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_285.variants.lb (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (S : Set ℕ)
    (hS : S = {k | ∃ (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ), StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧
      1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i })
    (h : ∀ k ∈ S,
      IsLeast
        { n (Fin.last k) | (n : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n)
          (_ : 1 = ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / n i) }
        (f k)) :
    ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
      ∀ k ∈ S, (1 + o k) * rexp 1 / (rexp 1 - 1) * (k + 1) ≤ f k := by
  sorry

end Erdos285

reformulations.difference: Lean uses k+1 denominators, specifies a total natural-valued minimum function only on the admissible-index set S, and expresses the asymptotic using an error sequence with equality at every admissible index.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: S is exactly ℕ \ {1}: a one-term representation exists, a two-term representation does not, and splitting the largest denominator in a representation of length at least three produces the next length. Thus f(k)=M_{k+1}(1) on S. The minimum hypotheses are satisfiable and uniquely determine these values. With c=e/(e−1)>0, the exact Lean conclusion is equivalent to f(t−1)/(ct) tending to 1 as t tends to infinity. Values at the finitely many exceptional indices do not affect this limit. The classification of S and this precise equivalence were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The asymptotic lower bound is expressed as an inequality at every admissible index using an existential little-o sequence, with the same k+1 indexing.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Because S contains all sufficiently large naturals and c=e/(e−1)>0, the exact conclusion is equivalent to: for every ε>0, eventually 1−ε ≤ f(k)/(c(k+1)). This is the usual asymptotic lower bound after reindexing. Conversely, such eventual bounds give a suitable error sequence o(k)=min(f(k)/(c(k+1))−1,0), which tends to zero and satisfies the inequality at every index. This equivalence was proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: Greg Martin, Denser Egyptian fractions, Acta Arith. 95 (2000), no. 3, 231–260. Read the LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9811112, especially the introduction's definition of M_t(r), the exceptional two-term case, Theorem 2, and its deduction in Section 2.

Greg Martin's website: https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/, https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/index.shtml?research, and https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/index.shtml?alph — navigation and confirmation of the publication citation.

Local definition sources: Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Defs.lean, Mathlib/Order/Monotone/Defs.lean, Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean and Lemmas.lean; Batteries/Util/ExtendedBinder.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: Both declarations were checked. Martin's Theorem 2 proves the stronger estimate M_t(1)=t/(1−e⁻¹)+O(t log log(3t)/log(3t)), supporting answer(True) and both research solved tags. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/285 was blocked by Cloudflare, so its current webpage annotations could not be read; the mathematical review used the cited primary paper instead. /workspace/review/complete_checks.lean compiles successfully and contains boundary checks, minimum-existence checks, the admissibility classification, and both equivalences. The principal verification lemmas have no sorry dependencies. The reviewed file was not modified.
